extracted.intended_audience: prospective subscribers/readers of the book 'Our Fathers Have Told Us' and readers interested in architectural and Christian history; potential supporters/patrons
extracted.subtask_description: Author's published plan for the multi-part book 'Our Fathers Have Told Us', specifying topical scope for each part, internal sectioning, illustration and museum-deposit policy, edition/distribution and subscription dependence. Useful for understanding production, editorial, and dissemination choices for this specific historical/architectural work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall work scope (ten parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The work, if I live to complete it, will consist of ten parts, each taking up some local division of Christian history, and gathering, towards their close, into united illustration of the power of the Church in the Thirteenth Century.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author lists intended focuses for each numbered part (first: early Frank power and Cathedral of Amiens; second: 'Ponte della Pietra' on Theodoric and Verona; third: 'Ara Celi' on foundations of Papal power; fourth: 'Ponte-a-Mare'; fifth: 'Ponte Vecchio' on Pisa and Florence; sixth: 'Valle Crucis' on English/Welsh monastic architecture; seventh: 'The Springs of Eure' on Chartres; eighth: 'Domrémy' on Rouen and related schools; ninth: 'The Bay of Uri' on Pastoral forms of Catholicism to modern times; tenth: 'The Bells of Cluse' on pastoral Protestantism of Savoy, Geneva, and the Scottish border).

rubrics_metrics.name: Part internal structure (four sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each part will consist of four sections only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the four sections, the fourth, will usually be descriptive of some monumental city or cathedral (i.e., a consistent internal architecture across parts: three preparatory chapters and a descriptive fourth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fourth section purpose (descriptive)
rubrics_metrics.description: One section of each part (usually the fourth) is to be descriptive of some monumental city or cathedral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes a recurring role for a descriptive, locality-focused section that ties the part's preparatory material to a concrete architectural example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustration policy (minimum per chapter)
rubrics_metrics.description: One illustration at least will be given with each chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings made for other illustrations will be placed at once in the Sheffield museum for public reference, and engraved as the author finds support, or opportunity for binding with the completed work. The extent and quality of engraved illustration depends on available support/subscribers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum-deposit and engraving contingency
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings made for illustrations will be placed in the Sheffield museum for public reference and engraved as the author finds support or opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations are staged: initial drawings are publicly deposited; full engraving/printing of them is contingent on financial/support circumstances and opportunities to bind them into the completed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edition and distribution policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A smaller edition of the descriptive chapters will commonly be printed in reduced form for travellers and non-subscribers; otherwise, the work is intended to be furnished to subscribers only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There will be at least two distribution channels: (a) reduced, smaller editions of descriptive chapters for travellers/non-subscribers; (b) the main (subscriber) edition for supporters—implying exclusivity of the full work to subscribers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription dependence for illustration and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The author invites subscription because the degree in which he can increase the work's usefulness by engraved illustration must greatly depend on the known number of its supporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical production decisions (number/quality of engraved plates, extent of illustration) are explicitly linked to subscription numbers; this is an appeal to patronage as a production constraint and criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index referencing convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in the case of Chapter 1., which is not divided into numbered sections, the references in this index are to both page and section. Thus 206. iv. 51 is to page 206, Chapter IV., § 51.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index entries follow the 'page. chapter_roman. section' pattern; users should interpret index locators accordingly (special-case: Chapter 1 lacks numbered sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic unity aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Each part gathers, towards their close, into united illustration of the power of the Church in the Thirteenth Century.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond local or sectional topics, the parts are intended to converge thematically to demonstrate a single historical thesis about the Church's power in the 13th century—authors/editors should maintain that throughline when composing or selecting material.
